title: Feedback outbox: reports survive a lost connection
description: What the feedback sheet does when the network is gone (a train, a tunnel, offline singleplayer): the report is saved on the device with its own id and write time, a chip counts what is waiting, and it goes out by itself when the connection is back (or with Send now), once. Mocked game and a mocked /api/feedback; the connection is cut with Playwright's setOffline. Desktop 1440x900 and phone 390x844. Regenerate with npm run screenshots -- GJ.

shots.heading: Offline: the sheet says so
shots.caption: No connection: a note under the form and the button reads Save to send later. The text stays editable.

shots.heading: Saved on this device
shots.caption: Submitting offline writes the report to IndexedDB (localStorage if that is blocked) and says: Saved on this device, will be sent when you are back online. The chip counts what is waiting. Nothing went to the server.

shots.heading: Pending chip and history
shots.caption: Reopening the sheet shows the waiting report in the small history (state, preview, age, tries). The game was never blocked.

shots.heading: Not sent: Send now
shots.caption: Back online, but the server refused the report (here a 400): it is marked Not sent and kept, with a 44 px Send now button. Timeouts, 5xx and 429 stay Waiting and retry with backoff (Retry-After honoured); 413 is Not sent at once.

shots.heading: Retry succeeded
shots.caption: Send now delivered the report: All sent, history says Sent. Every attempt carried the same report_id, so the server stores it once; it also carries client_queued_at (when it was written) and the attempt number.

notes.title: Not shown
notes.text: Automatic retry on the online event, on tab visibility and on page load, the backoff, 413 and 429 handling, several tabs (Web Locks plus BroadcastChannel) and gzip storage of a large save are covered by vitest (web/src/feedback/outbox.test.ts); the server's idempotency and client_queued_at by the Rust integration test.
